source_text: quam Thessalonicam miserunt ... in auxilium suum vel pro cattholica fide contra Manichaeorum, sicut loquuntur, profanitatem consensionem Orientalium episcoporum videntur exposcere ... damnant eos, quos praedixit Apostolus recessuros a fide, cauteriatam habentes conscientiam, prohibentes nubere, abstinentes a cibis, quos immundos putant, nec putantes a Deo cuncta esse condita ... omnis creatura Dei bona sit et nulla substantia sit, quam non summus fecerit Deus, nisi ipse Deus qui non est ab aliquo factus
pass_a_gloss: They sent the letter to Thessalonica, seeking the Eastern bishops' consent for help, or as they speak, for the catholic faith against Manichaean profanity. They condemn those who, as the Apostle foretold, will withdraw from the faith, having a seared conscience, forbidding to marry, abstaining from foods which they think unclean, and not thinking that all things were founded by God. Every creature of God is good, and there is no substance which the highest God did not make, except God himself who was not made by anyone.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: Augustine reports that Julian and several fellow bishops sent this letter to Thessalonica. They sought the Eastern bishops’ support “for the catholic faith against Manichaean impiety.” They condemned people who abandon the faith, have a seared conscience, forbid marriage, abstain from foods they consider unclean, and do not believe that everything was created by God (1 Timothy 4:1–4). Their position was that every creature of God is good, and that the supreme God made every substance except God himself, who was not made by anyone.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.
Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.
